decisive_items: An MRI of the hips and pelvis then demonstrated bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy
left hip pain worsened, strength declined to 2/5 at the hip and 3/5 at the knee
response.rationale: MRI directly shows bilateral iliopsoas muscle oedema and left insertional tendinopathy, matching the clinical hip flexor weakness and pain. Polymyalgia rheumatica is less specific and lacks the focal tendinopathy finding.

rejected.why: No erosive or symmetric joint pattern; joint effusion is nonspecific and aspiration unsuccessful.
Systemic inflammation and weight loss are present, but MRI shows focal iliopsoas tendinopathy rather than typical PMR bursitis pattern.
Gout history and presumed crystal arthropathy, but colchicine failed and no crystal confirmation; MRI findings are tendinopathic.
MRI ruled out abscess; no central canal stenosis or abscess.
MRI showed no central canal stenosis or cauda equina compression.
